scope: chapters 1-4 and 8-13, all 21 new entries; synthesis across the 43-entry Matthew 1-13 index

gaps_proposed.reason: PR22 is bearing with peevish or ungrateful behaviour from those one is helping; the tax collectors are welcoming him, and the Pharisees objecting are not being helped. PR10 is full participation in society while anchored elsewhere, which is a posture rather than a meal. The reviewer's phrase — cross-boundary mercy — is accurate and is not either definition. PR29 already carries the passage.

The man hides the treasure again before liquidating, which reads as a purchase strategy rather than secret faithfulness. Declined on the narrow reading of PR13. But the author has ruled that PR13 reaches the whole posture — the low place held without display — and under that broader reading the concealment becomes arguable. Left off and recorded rather than settled silently, because the broadening was the author's and so is this call.
gaps_proposed.author_ruling: Matthew 13:44 does not anchor PR13. The concealment is transactional, not a posture held without display.

running_tally: Twenty-six additions proposed across all books: ten accepted, one in part, fifteen declined.
reviewer_note: A third consecutive round in which every proposed addition was declined. The drafter's declines are themselves worth watching for reflex — each was checked against the definition rather than dismissed, and the 13:44-46 case was escalated rather than closed.
